role.altitude: The week is still the room: watching, explaining and keeping order. Less of it is retyping a header, a blank outline or a closed-item total.
reach: A mentor reads the observation sentence.
A co-teacher sees the accepted outline.
A pupil and a parent see a mark the teacher confirmed.
skills_to_grow: Reject an outline whose example is not the method they will show
Reject a suggested band the answer did not earn
Refuse a health or behavior sentence they did not see
role.ambitious_version: Before the lesson the outline they accepted is stored, closed marks they confirmed are summed, and the last observation is on the pupil. They still watch, still explain, and still decide what a breach means.

steps.what: Observe students' behavior, social development and physical health.
Read the last stored note for this pupil.
Evaluate students' performance and say what was seen.
Write the observation sentence on the open pupil record.
Tick which students were seen on the side tally.
Mail the mentor when health or behavior needs them.

tasks.design: Watching the class, judging performance, and telling the pupil stay as they are. The {OTHER} pupil record opens the last note this teacher stored for the pupil they tap, and a form fills pupil and class from the enrolment list so the teacher only writes the sentence of what they saw. No system watches the room or scores the pupil.
tasks.previous_blocker: The note was a fresh paragraph each time, and the last note sat in a file the teacher had to find.
tasks.enabler_now: A form on the pupil record can fill the header from the class list, and ordinary code can open the last note. The sentence is still the teacher's.
tasks.still_hard: Behavior, social development and physical health are seen in the room, and a wrong sentence about health is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the pupil and decides what the moment meant. A form cannot.
tasks.altitude: The week still has the full watch and the spoken judgement. The shorter piece is the header and the hunt for yesterday's note.

reach.task: Follow up a health or behavior note
reach.learn: The sentence says what the teacher saw, and who it was about.

reach.task: Read yesterday's note before the lesson
reach.learn: The note has the date and the area the teacher chose.

evidence.claim: Watching and judging are the bulk of this task. The digest has no measured saving on classroom observation.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned, so this design does not read emotion, behavior or physical health from a camera or a feed.
Storing the teacher's own sentence is not evaluating learning outcomes and is not watching a test.
ParnasSys keeps pupil records and names no AI. The form in this design sits on a record of that kind and does not score the pupil.

Under GDPR a public-task basis covers the note, a health sentence is special-category data, and a new pupil-data store needs a data-protection assessment. This is model knowledge, not a numbered digest source.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one class on one day. This is not an individual education plan and not the whole school curriculum. The room is in person, not a meeting, so the in-person share is 72 against a prior of 71.5 that was labelled as meetings.

Last-note contract, produced by this teacher on an earlier run of this same task: pupil, date, area and sentence. The first time the field is empty and they skip the read. Tapping the pupil opens that note, which is why the read drops to 50 percent; they still read it. Nothing watches the room.

Header contract on the write step: pupil and class are produced by enrolment, outside this task; the date is the day of the note. The teacher is the producer of the sentence, and that writing is the remaining 70 percent. If the class list is empty they type the header as well. The sentence is not a diagnosis.

Tally contract: the class list is produced by enrolment. If it is empty the teacher counts. The tick stays theirs, which is why the tally stays at 50 percent. Mentor mail is unchanged because the design does not shorten that writing. No second signature exists today.
Upkeep of 1 hour per 100 is correcting one note filed on the wrong pupil and adjusting the area list once a term. The per-note sentence stays in the write step.
unknowns: Whether this school's pupil record can store a note with pupil, date, area and sentence.
Whether mentors already receive a health or behavior note, and by mail.
research_questions: Does a header-filled note change how often the teacher writes the sentence?
Do mentors act on the sentence, and how often is it about the wrong pupil?

already_counted.description: Watching the class, unchanged.
The spoken judgement of what was seen, unchanged.
Writing the sentence of what was seen.
Reading the last note once it is open.
Ticking who was seen.
The mentor mail, unchanged.

incremental.description: Once a term, correct one note filed on the wrong pupil and adjust the area list. The sentence itself stays in the write step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A day of paper notes, and a pupil with no stored note, lands near 2. A day where every header fills and the last note opens lands near 5. The room stays full length.

steps.what: Open the goal for this subject before drafting.
Draft an outline for subjects such as English, mathematics or social studies.

loop.input: The chosen goal code and the method the teacher will show.
loop.output: An outline plus one worked example.
loop.check: The example is the method they will actually show, not a different method.
loop.stop: They reject it or accept it, and after two redrafts they write it themselves.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot phrase an example for a goal it has not seen.

steps.what: Confirm how many copies the class needs.
Instruct through lectures in this subject.
Lead the discussions and listen to the answers.
Give the demonstrations of the method on the board.
Send the co-teacher the stored outline link.

tasks.design: The lecture, the discussion and the demonstration stay as they are. Before the lesson, a draft outline and one worked example are made from the goal the teacher chose, and the teacher rejects any example that is not the method they will show. The curriculum owner supplies the goal list and enrolment supplies the class size on the {OTHER} pupil record; the teacher still reads the goal and still confirms the count.
tasks.previous_blocker: The outline started from a blank page, and the goal sat in a folder the teacher searched by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can phrase a worked example from a goal the teacher already chose, and the teacher accepts or rewrites it before the lesson.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the class followed the explanation is only visible in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher hears the wrong answer and changes the explanation. The draft cannot.
tasks.altitude: The lesson stays the same length. The shorter piece is a blank outline, and only when the teacher keeps the draft.

reach.task: See the outline before a shared lesson
reach.learn: The outline is the version the teacher accepted, with the example they will actually show.

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts a class activity for a lesson goal. This design drafts an outline the teacher accepts or rewrites, and it does not teach the lesson.
A Lucas Onderwijs pilot has the teacher accept or change a suggested arithmetic lesson. The live lesson here is not that pilot, and the source gives no minutes.
ChatGPT plus a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes, and a panel found no quality difference. That is planning, not the lecture, so it is not this task's saving.

Oak's Aila cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, covered 7 percent of lessons, use declined over ten weeks, and under one in five felt it influenced teaching. That is preparation. The live lesson stays full length, so the outline step keeps most of its time.
Drafting an outline is not evaluating learning outcomes and not watching the room.
A school that adapts the drafting tool can become its provider and must confirm that before the outline is used.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one subject, one lesson, this class. Not the whole curriculum and not an individual education plan. Lectures, discussions and demonstrations are in person (74 against a prior of 75.1 labelled as meetings). The prior chance of a clear gain is about preparation, which is the outline step, not the teaching hour.

Goal contract, produced by the curriculum owner outside this task: goal code, subject and year. The list opens on this subject and year, which is why the open step drops to 60 percent; they still read the goal. If the list is empty they read the curriculum document, and that reading stays in the step.

Class-size contract, produced by enrolment outside this task: the pupil count for this class. They confirm it and do not store a new number, which is why the confirm step drops only to 60 percent. If the field is empty they count.

Outline mechanism: a draft phrases one worked example from the goal they chose, and they accept or rewrite it before the lesson. Influence of drafted preparation is weak, so 80 percent of that step remains. The link step drops only because the stored link is inserted; they still write the one-line note. The lecture, the discussion and the demonstration stay at 100 percent.

No second signer exists today. The teacher is the only person who accepts the outline. Upkeep of 1.5 hours per 100 is rewriting one rejected outline by hand and rereading a sample of examples. Editing a kept draft is already in the outline step. The planning trials in the evidence are not the range for this task.
unknowns: Whether goal codes for this subject and year already sit on a list the teacher can open.
Whether a co-teacher needs the outline before a shared lesson.
research_questions: Do outlines the teacher accepted change what happens in the live lesson?
How often does the teacher reject the worked example because it is not the method they will show?

already_counted.description: Reading and rewriting the outline and the worked example.
The lecture, unchanged.
The discussion, unchanged.
The demonstration, unchanged.
Reading the goal once the list is open.
The one-line note to the co-teacher.
Confirming the copy count.

incremental.description: Rewrite one rejected outline by hand per 100 hours, and reread a sample of examples. Editing a kept draft is already in the outline step.

approvals.approved_version: The stored outline and worked example after the teacher has accepted or rewritten them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of blank-page outlines lands near 1. A week where one outline is accepted with light edits lands near 3. The lecture, the discussion and the demonstration stay full length.

steps.what: Prepare tests and assignments and write the key.

loop.input: The goal for this sitting and the item types the teacher will use.
loop.output: Draft items with a proposed correct option.
loop.check: Each item maps to the goal, and the correct option is the one the teacher will teach.
loop.stop: They reject the paper, or after two redrafts they write it themselves.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed item bank cannot phrase a question for a goal it has not seen.

steps.what: Administer tests by handing each paper out.
Watch students sit the test and notice trouble.
Collect the tests when the sitting ends.
Check closed-item marks against the stored key.
Grade open assignments and evaluate students' progress.

loop.input: The pupil's answer and the rubric.
loop.check: The teacher sees every answer, and the band matches what the pupil wrote, not only an item id.
loop.stop: Below the agreed agreement they mark by hand, and after two redrafts of a suggestion they mark that answer themselves.
loop.why_not_simpler: Ordinary code can add rubric points only after the band is confirmed. It cannot read whether the answer earned the band.

steps.what: Add the confirmed marks into the pupil total.
Send the confirmed total with the teacher's sentence.

tasks.design: The sitting stays as it is: the teacher hands out the paper, watches the room and collects the scripts. Closed items are compared to the key the teacher stored on the prepare step, and the teacher corrects any row on the wrong pupil before the mark is kept. Open answers get a suggested band, and the teacher reads every answer and changes any band the answer did not earn. The total is the sum of marks already confirmed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed items were added by hand, and an open answer had no suggested band to accept or reject.
tasks.enabler_now: Ordinary code can compare a selected option to a stored key and add confirmed marks. A bounded suggestion can propose a rubric band the teacher still checks against the answer.
tasks.still_hard: A mark that counts has to be the teacher's, and a suggested band can be wrong in a way that only the answer shows.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows what was taught and whether the answer earned the band.
tasks.altitude: The sitting stays the same length. Less time goes to adding closed items and re-adding a total the teacher already confirmed.

reach.task: See a mark that was confirmed
reach.learn: The total is the sum of marks the teacher confirmed, not a suggested band left as-is.
Any sentence in the message is one the teacher sent.

evidence.claim: CheckMate, from Cito, suggests scores for open questions. One of seven teachers in the pilot says 1.5 hours of marking took under 15 minutes. That is his account, not a measured saving. The teacher here still reads every open answer.
Teacher Tapp in October 2026 found 7 percent of secondary teachers use AI for marking, against 31 percent who expected to in 2023.

Texas rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026, and computers first scored 58 percent of 13,300+ raised reading scores. That is why a mark is not posted until the teacher has confirmed it.
Marks that count are high-risk from 2 December 2027. The teacher confirms each closed mark and each open band.
Inferring emotions is banned. The sitting stays with the teacher. Nothing watches the room.
A school that adapts the band suggestion can become its provider and must confirm that before a suggestion is shown.
Closed items can be compared to a stored key by ordinary code. The digest describes that pattern and gives it no source id.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one class, one sitting, this subject. Not a state exam and not an individual education plan. Handing out, watching and collecting are in person (46 against a prior of 46.3). Those three steps stay at 100 percent. Nothing watches the room.

Key contract, produced by the teacher on the prepare step of this task: item id, correct option and points. If the key is missing, closed items are marked by hand, and that is the low end of the range. The compare step stays with the teacher at 45 percent: code matches the selected option to that key, and the teacher corrects a row on the wrong pupil and a sample before the mark is kept.

Response contract: pupil id, item id and selected option are produced by the pupil during the sitting the teacher already watches. That answering is not extra pupil work and is not a new baseline. If the test stays on paper, the teacher marks from the script.

Open answers: a suggestion proposes a band only. The teacher reads every answer, which is why 80 percent of the grade step remains. Below the school's agreed agreement they mark by hand. The official mark is the teacher's write. The total step only adds marks already confirmed on the compare and grade steps, which is why it drops to 40 percent; they still check blank rows. It has no separate gate because those marks were already confirmed.

The result message drops only because the confirmed number is inserted. They still write the sentence, and they remove any judgement they did not confirm before it leaves the school. No second human signature exists today. Upkeep of 2.5 hours per 100 is a second look at a sample of closed items and rewriting one rejected paper. Reading every open answer is already in the grade step.
unknowns: Whether tests are on paper or a form that already stores the selected option.
Whether parents receive the result by mail, and the agreed agreement below which open answers are marked by hand.
research_questions: On this school's rubrics, how often does a suggested band match the band the teacher confirms?
How often is the key missing, so closed items are marked by hand?

already_counted.description: Checking the paper and writing the key.
Handing out the papers, unchanged.
Watching the sitting, unchanged.
Collecting the scripts, unchanged.
Correcting closed marks before they are kept.
Reading every open answer and confirming the band.
Checking blank rows on the total.
Writing the sentence that goes with the total.

incremental.description: Second-mark a sample of closed items and rewrite one rejected paper. Reading every open answer is already in the grade step.

approvals.approved_version: The stored paper and the key after the teacher has checked every item.
The closed marks after the teacher has corrected any row on the wrong pupil.
Each open band after the teacher has read the answer and confirmed or changed it.
The result message after the teacher has removed any sentence that adds a judgement they did not confirm.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A handwritten essay with no key, marked by hand, lands near 3. A class with a stored key, closed items on a form, and open answers the teacher still reads, lands near 9. The sitting stays full length.

steps.what: Establish rules and procedures for behavior in this class.
Tell students the rules and the procedures.
Notice a breach and decide what order requires.
Enforce the rules, maintaining order among students.
Record the incident against the rule that was broken.
Write to the parent when the procedure says so.

tasks.design: Stating the rules, noticing a breach and telling the pupil stay as they are. School leadership's rule list is copied forward, and the teacher writes only this class's lines. An incident form fills the pupil from the class list and the rule from those class lines, and the teacher still types what they saw and what they did. Nothing watches the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: The class rules were rewritten in full each term, and an incident note repeated the pupil's name and the rule.
tasks.enabler_now: The school rule list can be copied forward, and a form can fill the pupil and the rule from lists the school already keeps.
tasks.still_hard: What a breach means in that moment, and what will keep the room steady, is the teacher's call.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows the class and can tell a lapse from a pattern.
tasks.altitude: The room stays the same length. The shorter piece is rewriting the school list and retyping a pupil and a rule.

reach.learn: The class lines are the ones this teacher set on top of the school list.
The note says what the teacher saw and which rule it was.

evidence.claim: Inferring pupils' emotions is banned, so a breach is what the teacher noticed, not a score from a feed.
Works-council law does not apply to schools. Staff consent is required for a tool that can monitor them. This design does not monitor the room.
Under GDPR an incident note about a pupil is personal data, and a health or behavior sentence is not a diagnosis. Model knowledge, not a numbered digest source.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this class, this term. Not the whole school code and not an individual education plan. Telling the class, noticing a breach and keeping order are in person (86 against a prior of 85.6). Those steps stay at 100 percent. Nothing reads emotion and nothing watches the room.

School-rule contract, produced by school leadership outside this task: the standing rule list. Copying it forward is why the establish step drops to 65 percent; the teacher still writes this class's lines and still reads the list. If there is no list they write the class lines in full, and that is the low end of the range. The whole school code is not counted as time saved.

Incident contract: the pupil comes from the class list produced by enrolment; the rule comes from the class lines written on the establish step of this task. The teacher types what they saw and what they did, which is why 70 percent remains. If either list is empty they type those fields too.

Parent mail is unchanged in length and is gated because it leaves the school. No second signature exists today. Upkeep of 0.5 hours per 100 is moving one incident off the wrong pupil. Typing what was seen stays in the record step.
unknowns: Whether class rules are this teacher's lines on top of a shared school list, or rewritten in full.
Whether parents are meant to receive an incident note.
research_questions: Does copying the school list shorten the class-rules document, or do teachers still rewrite it?
How often is an incident filed against the wrong pupil or the wrong rule?

already_counted.description: Writing this class's lines and reading the school list.
Telling the class the rules, unchanged.
Noticing a breach and deciding what it means, unchanged.
Keeping order, unchanged.
Typing what was seen and what was done.
The parent note, unchanged.

incremental.description: Move one incident off the wrong pupil. Typing what was seen stays in the record step.

approvals.approved_version: The parent note after the teacher has written what they saw.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A term where the class rules are rewritten by hand lands near 0.5. A term where the school list is copied and only class lines are written lands near 2.5. The room stays full length.
